item.title: Leitrim facing long recovery from Storm Éowyn devastation
item.description: County Leitrim is among the areas facing the longest recovery from the devastation caused by Storm Éowyn. Earlier this week, Coillte confirmed forest clean-up operations will continue until at least mid-2027 The storm which occurred just under a year ago saw record wind speeds and unprecedented damage to the country's forestry sector. item.title: Leitrim councillors to grill ESB over storm damage
item.description: Elected representatives to Leitrim County Council are to quiz the ESB on their plans for its network in the county. Thousands of homes, farms and businesses were left without power for over three weeks following Storm Éowyn, while fallen trees impacted power lines across the county, making a number of regional and local routes impossible. Drumshanbo-based councillor Brendan Barry is hopeful answers will be found: Advertisement

item.description: Longford County Council has confirmed a major step forward for one of the town's most iconic buildings. The Connolly Barracks reimagined project has now entered the tender stage. Closed in 2009, the former barracks was bought by the local authority three years later. item.description: Ballymore continue to progress plans to turn Athlone into Ireland's first green city by 2040. The Ballymore Group wants to turn Athlone into a green city, with a population of 100,000 by 2040. item.title: Longford-Westmeath ETB building nearly complete
item.description: It's also been confirmed the new Longford-Westmeath Educational and Training Board (LWETB) building is nearing completion. The site, located at Connolly Barracks, will see the change of use of the former gymnasium building to educational use, among other measures. LWETB say they intend to expand its Further Education and training (FET) provision in Longford with the introduction of electrical apprenticeship training at the campus. item.title: 37 patients stranded on trolleys at Sligo hospital today
item.description: There were over 40 patients waiting for a bed at local hospitals this morning. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Friday's figures show there 37 patients waiting in Sligo University Hospital. Advertisement This included 26 in the emergency department and 29 on wards elsewhere. Meanwhile, there were three patients waiting at Portiuncula and two in the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar.

item.title: Thomas Smyth
item.description: Thomas Smyth Pakenhamhall Road, Castlepollard, Co. Westmeath and Ballintubber, Co. Roscommon. Thomas Smyth passed away on Thursday, January 22nd 2026. item.title: Hoped a solution can be found for Rathcroghan Farming Project
item.description: It's hoped that all parties can come together to find a solution for Rathcroghan Farming Project. Earlier this week, it announced it to cease operations in March due to a lack of long-term funding. The award-winning initiative has supported 90 farmers in managing more than 260 archaeological sites over the past eight years. Cllr Liam Callaghan feels the role of the project cannot be ignored: Advertisement

item.title: Funding announced for Elphin Windmill welcomed locally
item.description: Elphin Windmill has been allocated funding under the Heritage Investment Scheme. From rural areas and rural villages, the scheme helps protect historic structures, enhance streetscapes and keep traditional building skills alive for future generations. The sails were torn off the 300-year-old structure during the deadly Storm Éowyn. It has been a popular tourist attraction since it was restored almost 30 years ago. item.title: Local priest says schools play a huge role in keeping religion alive
item.description: A local priest says schools play a huge role in keeping religion alive in 2026. Local schools in the Shannonside region have been celebrating Catholic Schools week in many different ways. Ardagh/Moydow priest Fr. Vinny Connaughton has been visiting schools across the region and this morning he held a service for the students of Glen National School and their grandparents. He said weeks and events like this are crucial for keeping young people engaged in religion: Advertisement
